lines.en: Step by step, I head for the pasture.
My great horn hangs low before me.
My hooves leave deep prints.
The Pliocene wind is chill.
This bulk makes even walking hard work.
I move slowly along the riverbank.
The hair on my back brushes the grass.
My horn tip nearly scrapes the ground.
A kinsman trails not far behind.
I push a blocking shrub aside.
The ground thuds beneath me.
I sway with each step, but steady.
I head for the soft grass by the water.

lines.zh: 冷空气从我鼻孔里喷出来。
lines.en: Cold air plumes from my nostrils.
I go around that mud pit.

lines.zh: 我的蹄印比这条路还老。
lines.en: My hoofprints are older than this path.
Too heavy to turn late.
The herd has kept up.
I stand like a boulder.
A bird has landed on my horn.
I finish chewing my last mouthful.
The wind ruffles my coat.
I turn my head slowly.
No threat in this pasture.
I snort once.
A kinsman grazes in the distance.
I let my weight settle on four legs.
My hide is thick enough for the flies.
Light slides down one side of my horn.
I close my eyes a moment.
You stand right in front of my horn.
I look up at you, unimpressed.
You are small, like a bird.
I smell what is in your hand.
I lower my head, horn toward you.
Do not touch the horn; it is sharp.
I shift half a step to make room.
Stand back; I turn slowly.
We size each other up.
I cannot read your intent.
You have taken another step.
One of my ears swivels.
I give a low grumble.
I am large, but you need not fear.
I grunt and pull away.
A cut opens in my hide.
A numbness runs to the base of my horn.
I turn too slowly and pay for it.
This pain makes me want to charge.
I plant all four legs and hold.
Do not come at me again.
The beast beside me is watching.
I shake my head hard once.
The wound stays hot and burning.
That grass smells tender.
Lower the grass a bit.
I shift my enormous body.
Worth a few steps, for that.
I curl my tongue out once.
That smell makes me forget my aching horn.
One more step forward.
There is not enough grass in your hand.
My nose reaches it first.
I will follow, but slowly.
You hit my horn and fall back.
I barely moved a step.
I am too heavy to shove.
You stepped by my hooves.
I lean aside a little.
That annoyed me.
Do not come at me from the horn side.
Dust flies where we meet.
You retreat; I stop.
Remember to go around me next time.
I tilt my horn aside so it cannot hurt you.
We graze side by side.
You lean on me for warmth.
I nudge your shoulder with my nose.
This pasture belongs to us.
On long walks I take the outer side.
I answer with a low sound.
Even a one-horned beast has gentle hours.
You are slow, so I go slower.
We guard this ground together.
I flick it up with my horn.
I lower my head and take the bundle.
Something is caught on my horn.
I curl it into my mouth.
Tough; I chew it slowly.
I toss it onto my back.
I press it into the soil.
I will bring this to the young.
Another one snagged on my horn.
I carry it and turn slowly.
I raise my head and level my horn at you.
My horn points your way.
My hoof keeps pawing the dirt.
I have decided not to back away.
The one beside me lifts its head too.
This time we will not run.
You have made me lower my head.
My breathing deepens.
One more step, and the horn comes.
I watch the weapon in your hand.
I close in, one heavy step at a time.
One step back from you, one forward from me.
The ground shakes with me.
My kinsman stands at my flank.
I need no burst of speed.
The horn on my head is long enough.
I wait for you to come too close.
Another step back and you reach the water.
I press my head lower.
Do not circle behind; I can see you.
My horn tip drove in.
I charge with my whole head.
This blow can pierce through.
My forehooves come down together.
The blow lifts you off the ground.
I toss my head and fling you aside.
My horn is already bloodied.
I growl low and step back half a pace.
Do not think I only retreat.
This is how we answer.
I come down the grassy slope.
My great horn breaks the morning mist.
The Pliocene giant has arrived.
The ground begins to beat.
I halt and blow out a white breath.
This pasture has a new master.
My kin emerge one by one behind me.
My horn tip sweeps the grass.
My shadow stretches long.
I lift a foot and drop it hard.
Hoofbeats sound in the distance.
Did you hear that low bellow?
A patch of my coat is scorched.

lines.zh: 我重重砸在地上,起不来
lines.en: I crash down and cannot rise at once.

lines.zh: 水深过我的背,我喘不上气
lines.en: The water is over my back; I cannot breathe.
The blast rolls me onto my side.
An arrow is lodged in my shoulder.
That force runs straight up my horn.
My stomach is hollow and uneasy.
Lightning strikes my horn; my whole body jolts.

lines.zh: 脚下空了,我这么重也浮着
lines.en: No ground, and even my weight floats.
